definition: Opaque means hard to see through or understand.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word opaque. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know opaque should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Decades of smoke had turned the workshop's windows opaque, so the glassblower worked in a permanent amber dusk.
Hazy is the mildest rung — detail softens but the shapes still come through; it stops far short of opaque.
Murky stops short of opaque: you still catch dim outlines through murky water, while opaque means nothing passes at all.

Inscrutable belongs to faces, expressions, and people — the poker player's inscrutable stare gives nothing away. Opaque covers things: glass, prose, budgets, rules. Both refuse entry, but you meet an inscrutable person, while you stare at an opaque surface.

Cloudy means hazed over, swirled with particles or doubt, yet often thin enough to see through — cloudy water still shows the coins on the bottom. Opaque is the full stop: no light, no meaning, nothing gets past the surface at all.
letting light and meaning straight through
so easy to look through you forget it's there
Opaque is Latin opacus, 'shaded, dark' — the deep shade under trees. English borrowed it whole; apart from opacity, its own noun, it left no relatives to find.
Opaque means hard to see through or understand.
The poet's late notebooks are famously opaque: private symbols, dates that match no calendar, and marginal notes in a shorthand she taught to no one.
Opaque works on two levels — light cannot pass through an opaque pane, and meaning cannot pass through an opaque rule or report; either way, you are left staring at a surface.
Opaque works literally (glass, water) and figuratively (rules, prose, finances) — in both, nothing gets through.
Its unit-mate abstruse concedes there is depth to reach; opaque suggests the surface itself refuses you.

Every generation of fans takes a turn at 'Glass Harbor,' the band's most famous song, and every generation gives up.
The verses name no place, no year, and no one; the chorus swears 'the anchor knows' and refuses to say what.
Fan forums have produced three hundred rival readings, and not one of them survives contact with the second verse.
Critics who admire the melody still call the words opaque: you can press your ear against them for a decade and no meaning comes through.
The band's drummer once offered the only official explanation: 'It's about four minutes long.'
